body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

<!-- sparq-direct-5183-reference-reduction-v1 -->
Investigated the first mismatch, seed `4141222487`, from [the advancing UPDATE run on main `781f667c`](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/actions/runs/34458877088/job/102811674711). The following two-operation reduction exposes a reference-engine cardinality difference:

```sparql
INSERT DATA {
  <http://ex/s2> <http://ex/p1> "8"^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer> .
  <http://ex/s2> <http://ex/p1> "008"^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer> .
};
INSERT { ?s <http://ex/p0> _:bt }
WHERE { ?s <http://ex/p1> ?o }
```

Actual raw public-API results, without a canonicalizer:

| Input literals | Sparq: stored terms / WHERE rows / new blank nodes | Oxigraph 0.5.9: same counts |
|---|---|---|
| `8` and `008` | 2 / 2 / 2 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| `8` only | 1 / 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| `8` and `9` | 2 / 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 / 2 |

Sparq produced the same results through rebuild and in-place updates in both preserved default-feature builds, whose engine/core source provenance was checked against the revisions before and after #6478. The reference was built offline with the repository-pinned Oxigraph `0.5.9`, `rdf-12` only, and vendored spargebra `0.4.6`; dependency versions were unchanged. Its raw store iteration already contains only canonical `8` before the second operation. The numeric encoder parses valid integer lexical forms into an integer value and reconstructs the canonical literal on output.

[RDF literal identity includes lexical form](https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-concepts/#section-Graph-Literal), and [INSERT template blank nodes are fresh per WHERE solution](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-update/#deleteInsert). This explains the reduced difference before canonicalization: final literal normalization cannot undo the different number of newly generated blank nodes.

The original first seed has now been replayed once on each exact revision: pre-#6478 `d41ec9fcb796504d85f5a5247a5fdc9eb3e65de5` and post-#6478 `781f667c19a8ebb779cfccb24b05ea432360b025`. Both generated the identical ten-operation CI sequence and failed at zero-based index **8**, with the same extra `008` literal and blank-node-bearing quad. The strict Sparq rebuild-versus-in-place comparison passed before the reference comparison failed. Index 9 was generated but not executed after that failure. This particular witness therefore predates #6478 under the qualified diagnostic configuration.

The replay used the unchanged original module, parser, LOAD sandbox, allowlist and comparison guards, with the relevant engine/core/canon feature closure and pinned dependency versions preserved. It ran on macOS/aarch64 with a diagnostic optimized profile and one Rayon thread, rather than the exact Linux `release-fast` CI environment. **The other seven reported seeds remain unexecuted and their causes are not established.**

Independent Claude Opus 5 review supports the first-seed reference lexical-collapse explanation: the current comparator is correctly rejecting a residual cardinality difference. The proposed repair direction is to restrict the generated combinations that the reference cannot distinguish, strengthen lexical comparisons, and retain the original shape as an explicit Sparq regression. The remaining helper functions and probe semantics are being audited before any implementation. No engine, generator, comparator, canonicalizer or gate has been changed, and no mismatch has been waived.


### Remaining original cases and PR #6482

All seven remaining seed markers were reproduced once each on both `d41ec9f` and `781f667`, using the unchanged original generator and pinned dependency artifacts. Failure bodies and reconstructed sequences match across revisions. These are deterministic reconstructions: CI retained only the seven seed markers, not their full request text.

The failing zero-based indices are `4141222535:7`, `4141222571:9`, `4141222576:8`, `4141222599:5`, `4141222612:6`, `4141222617:5`, and `4141222622:4`. Every sequence inserts both `8` and `008` at `s2/p1` before the fresh-blank-node INSERT. Each observed delta is consistent with the same reference lexical-collapse/cardinality mechanism as the first seed. Actual independent Claude Opus5 xhigh review supports that grouping with qualifications; these seven did not add direct per-step WHERE-count instrumentation.

The original comparator explicitly adjudicates earlier lexical-only differences by normalization; the later extra blank-node structure remains a mismatch. Thus earlier reference comparisons passing does not mean their raw terms were identical. Strict Sparq-versus-Sparq comparison runs first and remains separate.

The repaired generator and stricter lexical adjudicator are now in [PR #6482](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/pull/6482), with the exact first historical sequence retained as a Sparq-only regression. Local Rust 2021 validation and independent source review passed; normal protected CI and merge remain required. The identical-lexical strict-comparison coverage gap raised during review is tracked separately in #6483.

This issue stays open pending the landed repair. The trailing ADD requests in `4141222612` and `4141222617` were not executed after their first mismatch. No claim is made that the original lexical-alias inputs now pass against the lossy reference, that engine semantics changed, or that passing the same numeric seeds under the new generator replays the originals.
